reachabilityOfMutatingPaths.conclusion: From VerifyPromotionReady.run() NO state-mutating path of the parent is reachable. Establishing facts:
facts: Every mutating parent member (_phase1..._phase6, _phase4d, _phase8_previewSmokeTests, _writeProgressFileWithStatus, _collectNudgeFromOwner, _moveBPT, _swapUniboost, _rescueTo, _migrateStaker) is `internal` — not externally callable, and the subclass's run() calls none of them.
The only external/public members of the base are `run()` (overridden) and `setUp() public view` (require chainid==1 only), plus compiler-generated public getters for constants/state (all view).
vm.startBroadcast / vm.startPrank / vm.deal / vm.warp appear ONLY inside those unreachable internal phase functions. There is no broadcast context opened anywhere on the verifier's path.
vm.writeFile appears ONLY in _writeProgressFileWithStatus (:2230), which the verifier never calls. No file is written by the verify leg.
The verifier IS invoked without --broadcast (npm key `promotion-ready:verify`), so even a hypothetical queued call would not be dispatched.

test/VerifyPromotionReadyGuards.t.sol pins the read-only property at SOURCE level (asserts absence of startBroadcast/startPrank/vm.deal/vm.warp/Test.sol import and of any OLD_POOLER reference in the verifier file).
residualExposure: The verifier still INHERITS StdCheats and the fs_permissions read-write grant on ./server/deployments; the capability exists in the compiled artifact even though the code path does not use it. Any future edit to VerifyPromotionReady that calls an inherited phase helper would silently regain broadcast/file-write reach — the guard test's source-scan is the only structural backstop, and it scans only for cheatcode literals, not for calls to inherited mutating helpers (e.g. a call to `_writeProgressFileWithStatus(...)` would pass every current assertion).

forge script's `--sig` can select any external function. The base exposes only view externals besides run(), so `--sig` cannot reach a mutating path today — but this is a property of the current member set, not an enforced invariant.

`_requireNoBroadcastFlag()` is named for a check it cannot perform: there is no cheatcode reporting --broadcast, so it only rejects PREVIEW_MODE. Its own NatSpec says so. A verify run mistakenly given --broadcast would not be caught by this function (it would still be inert, because no broadcast context is opened).

The verifier's `setUp()` is inherited and requires chainid == 1, so it cannot be run against a fork with a different chain id — relevant to any fork-based replay the script-auditor plans (a mainnet fork keeps chainid 1, so this is satisfiable).
